description: Patients who have at least one examination whose recorded ANA pattern is something other than S.

b.request: For patients who have at least one examination with a non-null `ANA Pattern` other than 'S', list the patient ID, sex (from Patient), and the unrounded average `aCL IgM` across all of that patient's examinations (ignoring nulls), grouped by ID and sex, sorted by average descending with null averages last, top 10.
b.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Examination WHERE `ANA Pattern` IS NOT NULL AND `ANA Pattern` <> 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL), AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10
b.raw: For patients who have at least one examination with a non-null `ANA Pattern` other than 'S', list the patient ID, sex (from Patient), and the unrounded average `aCL IgM` across all of that patient's examinations (ignoring nulls), grouped by ID and sex, sorted by average descending with null averages last, top 10.

d.request: Among patients who have at least one examination whose `ANA Pattern` is not 'S', list each patient's ID, sex (from the Patient table), and the unrounded average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations, ignoring nulls. Group by ID and sex, sort by the average descending with nulls last, and show the top 10.
d.sql: SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(E.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient P JOIN Examination E ON E.ID = P.ID WHERE P.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Examination WHERE `ANA Pattern` <> 'S') GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(E.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL) ASC, AVG(E.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For patients with at least one examination record whose `ANA Pattern` is recorded and is something other than 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
a.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_igm FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Examination WHERE `ANA Pattern` IS NOT NULL AND `ANA Pattern` <> '' AND `ANA Pattern` <> 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL), avg_igm DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Among patients whose examinations don't show an `ANA Pattern` of 'S', list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `aCL IgM` across all of their examinations (ignoring missing values, unrounded). Group by patient ID and sex, sort by that average from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10. Patients who have at least one examination whose recorded ANA pattern is something other than S.
